meta.grounding: Initial brief grounded in the five processed feeds. Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and run `node src/refresh.mjs` to regenerate live with Claude. Every figure traces to primary NYC data; interpretation is clearly hedged.

headline: New construction is accelerating into a cooling sales market, while operating risk climbs fastest in the same outer-borough neighborhoods.
summary: Citywide, New Building filings ran 1,536 in July 2026 (+24% year-over-year), yet recorded sales fell to 3,921 in May (−15% YoY) even as the median held near $940,000. That supply-up / demand-soft divergence is sharpest in a handful of ZIPs. Meanwhile hazardous-violation risk and 311 complaints (+21% YoY) concentrate in the Bronx and central Brooklyn, and Local Law 97 carbon exposure — roughly $759M per year today — is overwhelmingly a Manhattan large-building problem.

insights.title: Supply is outrunning demand in specific outer-borough ZIPs
insights.detail: Greenpoint (11222) filed 78% more New Building applications year-over-year while sales fell 44%; Bay Ridge (11209) shows +67% supply against −47% demand. The divergence is real in the data (fact). It suggests these pockets may face pricing pressure and rising concessions as pipeline units deliver into thinner buyer demand (interpretation).

insights.title: Low volume, firm pricing — a stalemate market
insights.detail: Sales are down 15% YoY citywide, but the median held at $940,000 and Manhattan's median rose 9% YoY. This pattern looks more like sellers holding and fewer transactions clearing than a broad price correction — worth watching whether firm pricing persists as inventory ages.

insights.title: 311 complaints are leading violations higher
insights.detail: Building complaints to 311 rose 21% YoY citywide, well ahead of the 4% rise in hazardous HPD violations — and complaints tend to precede violations. Immediately-hazardous violations are rising fastest in Canarsie (11236) and Greenwich Village-West (10014).

insights.title: Local Law 97 exposure is concentrated in Manhattan
insights.detail: About 73% of benchmarked buildings already exceed the tighter 2030 carbon limits, and estimated penalties total roughly $759M/year today — of which Manhattan is about $381M. For large-building owners this is a material, escalating compliance cost that most cannot easily self-compute, making it the highest-leverage risk to underwrite now.

neighborhoods.narrative: A construction surge — New Building filings up 78% year-over-year — is meeting a 44% drop in sales, with 495 immediately-hazardous violations logged this quarter. The widening supply/demand gap is worth watching for pricing softness as pipeline units deliver.
Sales cooled 27% year-over-year while the borough's development pipeline stayed elevated — a submarket where borough-level averages mask a genuine demand slowdown.

The city's heaviest concentration of habitability risk: 23,033 immediately-hazardous HPD violations this quarter. This reads as a standing stock problem rather than a sudden spike — a persistent operating-risk consideration for owners in these ZIPs.
Home to roughly $381M of the city's estimated annual Local Law 97 penalty exposure, with about 75% of covered buildings already over the 2030 limit — the dominant forward compliance cost in the city.
